## Current focus

Release verification for 1.0.0 (plan milestone M7): matrix runs, `docs/TESTING.md`, jar inspection.

## Roadmap

- [ ] Hands-on difficulty and timing trials with real players (the reference bots only prove the games are winnable).
- [ ] Dedicated server with two real clients: contention, latency (0/100/200 ms), reduced TPS, forged packets.
- [ ] Use brew-profile `presentation.accent` / `particle` (synced, not drawn yet).
- [ ] Later content (spec 30): herb drying, poultices, coatings, fermentation, alchemist jewelry.

## Decisions

- Quality never edits canonical potion contents; it lives in the `immersive_brewing` stack compound and is resolved
  where effects apply (five verified mixins, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` ADR-1).
- One logical step per server tick (50 ms); clients send input frames only (ADR-2).
- Every material has one owner: job ledgers move reserved stacks out of public slots; breaking packages the ledger
  whole, even during the count-in (ADR-3).
- Plans are validated against the brewing registry through adapters; data can describe, never invent, a transformation.
- Sister mods are optional and isolated: Smithing via IMC + conditioned data, Tanning data only, Enchanting and Jewelry
  coexistence only.
- Version strings live only in `gradle.properties` (mods.toml ranges are expanded from it).
- The help overlay pauses every game, practice included (playtest feedback): the client stops stepping and sends
  `PauseSessionC2S`; the server stops the session clock when it arrives. The resume carries the client's next step
  and remaining count-in, and the server re-anchors `runStartTick` from those (`SessionManager.RESUME_SLACK`), never
  from arrival times: anchoring on arrival times let a pause handled late start the run early and drop frames as
  late (smoke test: mortar extraction 63 instead of 100, back to 100 after). Closing the help mid-run counts in
  `ClientSession.RESUME_TICKS` on the client before the resume is sent. Protocol version 2.
- The Kettle's draft steps with `W`/`S` (`DRAFT_UP`/`DRAFT_DOWN`) instead of absolute `1`/`2`/`3` keys, like the
  Alembic's valves (playtest: too many keys at once); the screen shows each key on the level it selects next.
- Apothecary, More Potions, PotionsMaster and RPG Potions are data only: `compat/<modid>/` plans, reagent profiles,
  effect policies and Alembic recipes behind `forge:mod_loaded` (definition files take Forge conditions), generated by
  `tools/generate_data.py`; jars in `libs/` are compile-only, dev runtime with `-PwithX` or `-PwithPotionMods`.
- The Forge adapter refuses loose registry matches (`RegistryQuery`): a plain `BrewingRecipe` brews only the potion its
  declared input names, though a stand accepts any potion of that container (RPG Potions).
- The Kettle completes its bounded catalog (512 plans per input) with the paths its tray can pay for
  (`PlanIndex.plansUsing`, same bound); the Notebook lists only client-validated paths.

## Known issues

- First-person drinking animation follows the item's own 32 ticks even when quality changes the use time (cosmetic).
- Effect-quality handlers are consulted on drink and splash paths only; other mods' items stay metadata-only in
  lingering clouds and on arrows (API v1 limitation, documented).
- Apothecary's plans follow its config defaults: a changed ingredient leaves that plan unsupported (the new step is a
  contextual query). With More Potions too, a magma block on Awkward is Fire, so Apothecary's Burning plan is
  unsupported (a stand behaves the same). Its six recipes that need Iron's Spellbooks (Mana Regeneration and Mana
  Exhaustion) have no plans.
- Under a tiling window manager the client smoke test needs `tools/run_smoke_matrix.sh` to size its window; a plain
  `runClient -PsmokeTest` uses whatever size the compositor gives.
